title: Intelligent anchored placement with residency escrow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and implement an anchored placement strategy plus a 'residency escrow' mechanism for regional and multi-zone dedicated fleets. The goal is to provide predictable throughput allocations (guarantees) while enabling safe autoscale/shrink behaviour during zone pressure and planned maintenance, without violating data residency constraints. This ticket covers scheduler policy extensions, admission controls, a residency token escrow API, and operator-visible metrics and runbook steps for controlled failover and spillback.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler honors residency escrow tokens when satisfying placement decisions for dedicated pools in a region (can pin up to X% of capacity per-residency token)
Autoscaler respects throughput guarantees: scaling down does not evict pinned residency tokens until a configurable grace window expires
Failover procedure can spill requests to compatible zones only when residency escrow permits; otherwise requests are rejected with clear error codes and guidance
Control-plane and Console surfaces show per-pool escrowed capacity, current usage, and predicted eviction windows
E2E test harness simulates zonal outage and demonstrates controlled spillback without residency leakage (test coverage in CI)
Docs: Runbook + API doc published to Confluence and SDK helper included in node/python clients
updates: 2026-01-18: Ticket created by Maya to capture multi-zone residency failures observed in recent customer engagement. Initial design proposal linked.

2026-01-21: Architecture sync — decided on escrow token model (short-lived tokens that reserve throughput units) rather than hard node pinning to avoid underutilization. Noted trade-offs: small risk of temporary overcommit if tokens expire during sudden traffic surge.

notes: Residency escrow concept: allocate 'throughput credits' tied to residency constraints (region/zone/data-class) that the scheduler consumes instead of node-level pins. Credits have TTL and can be extended by heartbeat.

Throughput guarantees modeled as minimum reserved credits per customer pool. Autoscaler reduces non-reserved capacity first; only after grace windows can reserved credits be revoked based on policy (e.g., emergency-shrink vs scheduled-maintenance).

Compatibility: When spilling to a different zone, the runtime must verify model variant compatibility (quantization/arch) before accepting traffic. If incompatible, the request should failover to a fallback model or return a clear 409-style error.
Operator UX: Console exposes 'Escrow Overview' with timeline bars for each pool, predicted eviction times, and recommended mitigation (prewarm, increase reserves, enable cross-zone failover).
SLO considerations: Provide a new SLA dimension describing residency-bound throughput availability and acceptable failover latency when escrow permits spill.
Trade-offs discussed: token-based approach reduces scheduling complexity and improves packing but requires robust bookkeeping and KMS-signed tokens to prevent tampering.
Risk: Long-lived tokens could cause capacity fragmentation. Mitigation: automatic rebalancer job and token expiry heuristics that drop oldest low-utilization tokens first.
